The Moon mystery

How do we see a source of light?

A source of light gives out its own light. Its light travels in straight lines. When some of that light reaches us, we can see the source.
Ben looks at a lamp, which is a source of light. Which picture shows how Ben sees the lamp? Circle it.

Light Explorer · Mission 35 / 14

Seeing things that are not sources

Most things are not sources of light. We see them because light from a source hits them and reflects off them. Some of that light comes to us.
How does Glow see the book? Write 1, 2 or 3 to put the steps in order.
The light reflects off the book.
The reflected light goes into Glow's eyes.
The lamp gives out light.
Ray drawing. Draw rays with arrows to show how the girl sees the parrot.
Fill in the blank.

Light bounces off the parrot. We say the parrot light.

Source or not?

Some things give out their own light. Other things only reflect light. Careful! Shiny things can look bright, but that does not make them sources.
Sort them. Write each thing in the correct column.
a mirror · the Sun · the Moon · a firefly · a white wall · a candle flame · a disco ball · a TV that is on
Gives out its own lightOnly reflects light
At a party, a disco ball sparkles. Ploy says it is a source of light. Is she right? Explain.
Write one thing in your home that reflects light but is not a source.
Light Explorer · Mission 37 / 14

Can we see in the dark?

To see an object, we need light and our eyes. Light has to travel from the object to us. No light, no seeing!
Science story. Long ago, many people believed that our eyes sent out light to see things. About 1,000 years ago, a scientist called Ibn al-Haytham showed that light travels into our eyes.
Circle the correct word.

In a room with no light at all, we cancannot see a red ball.

Glow switches off every light in a room with no windows. Why can't he see his book?
How does a dark room show that Ibn al-Haytham was right?
Light Explorer · Mission 38 / 14

Mirror or board?

Every object reflects some light. Smooth, shiny surfaces like mirrors send the light off neatly in one direction. Rough, dull surfaces spread the light out in many directions.
Sharif shines a torch at a mirror. Majid shines a torch at a wooden board. Who sees a bright spot of light on the wall?

SharifMajid sees a bright spot.

Circle the three things that reflect light best.
a wooden boarda mirrorkitchen foila towela carpeta shiny spoon
Why can you see yourself in a mirror but not in a wooden door?
Light Explorer · Mission 39 / 14

Can light pass through?

Transparent materials let almost all light through. Translucent materials let only some light through. Opaque materials let no light through.
tracing paper
wood
clear glass
Label each material. Use the words in the box.
opaque · transparent · translucent

1   2   3

Match each word to what it means. Write the letter.
1.transparenta. Some light passes through. Things look blurry.
2.translucentb. Light bounces off it.
3.opaquec. We can see clearly through it.
4.reflects lightd. No light passes through it.
Glow shines a torch at tracing paper. What will he see on the other side?
